S66.01.needs: a GitHub App installation or a public GitHub repository URL; a cloud sandbox may not start until the deployment gate in the plan is switched on
S66.01.note: The picker only lists repositories when a GitHub App is configured; otherwise only a public URL works (copy in code-surface.ts). Whether a session then runs is not judged here.
steps: Sign in and open Code (the /code page).
In the new-session composer, click the "Select repository" chip.
Pick a repository from the list, or click "Use a repository URL instead" and type an owner/repository URL.
Click "Use this repository".
Look for the chosen repository name on the composer chip and compare with Expected (the repository is chosen before the session starts).
S66.01.where: Code > new session composer > "Select repository" chip > "Repository URL" or the list, then "Use this repository"

S66.02.note: A cloud branch field is shown with the repository; the desktop local folder shows branch names through its own chip. Branch switching copy says the branch is checked out in place.
steps: Open Code and choose a repository as in S66.01.
Read the "Branch" field, or click the branch chip and choose a branch from the "Branches" list.
Type a branch name in "Search or type a branch name" if needed, then click "Use this branch".
Compare the branch shown on the chip with Expected (the session starts from that git branch).
S66.02.where: Code > new session composer > "Select repository" > "Branch" field, or "Change the branch" > "Use this branch"

S66.04.needs: a Desktop folder for the Local option; a signed-in account for Cloud
S66.04.note: The Local option appears in the desktop composer menu (CodeComposer.tsx) only; the web Cloud path is the default. Environment labels are in code-surface.ts.
steps: Open Code and look at the new-session composer.
Click the environment chip (it shows "Cloud" or "Local" with the network mode).
In the menu, choose "Local" (runs in a chosen folder on this computer) or "Cloud" (runs in an isolated cloud sandbox).
Check that the chip now shows the choice, and compare with Expected (chosen before the session starts).
S66.04.where: Code > new session composer > environment chip > "Local" or "Cloud"

S66.05.needs: at least one earlier cloud session (empty state shows "No cloud sessions yet.")
S66.05.note: On the desktop app a second list, "On this device", shows local sessions (LOCAL_CODE_COPY in apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts).
steps: Open Code.
Look at the session list on the left under "Cloud sessions".
Use the "Filter sessions" menu or "Search sessions" to narrow the list if needed.
Click a session title to open it.
Compare the list and the opened session with Expected (a list of the user's sessions that can be opened).
S66.05.where: Code > left list "Cloud sessions" (sessions group) > click a session title

S66.06.needs: a cloud session you can open
S66.06.note: The "Session actions" button is icon-only, so testers must find it by position at the top of the session. Desktop renaming is a separate title control (LocalSessionTitleInput.tsx).
steps: Open a cloud session from the session list.
Click the session actions button at the top of the session (it has no visible text; its accessible name is "Session actions").
Click "Rename".
Type a new title in the "Session title" field and click "Rename the session" (or "Keep the current title" to cancel).
Compare the title shown in the list and header with Expected (a readable title that can be renamed).
S66.06.where: Code > open a session > "Session actions" icon menu > "Rename" > type title > "Rename the session"

S66.07.needs: sessions in different states (a running one is hard to set up on demand)
S66.07.note: Only part of the status set is shown: Running, Ready and Idle groups and the closed banner. Failed sessions are grouped as Idle, and no separate "Waiting for approval" session label was found in code-surface.ts.
steps: Open Code and look at the session list.
Find sessions under the group heading "Ready" or "Idle", and any running dot labelled "Running".
Open a session and read its status line or banner.
Compare with Expected (running, waiting for approval, idle, failed or closed).
S66.07.where: Code > left list ("Cloud sessions") > group headings "Running", "Ready", "Idle", and the "Open" badge; closed sessions show the banner "This session is closed."

S66.15.needs: a cloud session with its environment running
S66.15.note: The cloud Terminal is in CodeChangesPanel.tsx. The desktop version is a bottom panel with terminal tabs (LocalTerminal.tsx). The "Changes" button that opens this panel in cloud sessions was not traced to its trigger.
steps: Open a cloud session.
Open the "Changes" panel.
Scroll to the "Terminal" section.
Type a short command (for example ls) in the "Command" field and click "Run".
Compare the output that appears in the Terminal with Expected (the command output is shown in the session).
S66.15.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Terminal" section > "Command" field > "Run"

labels.text: No commands have run in this session.

S66.17.needs: a session where commands have already run
S66.17.note: The desktop equivalent is the "Running in this folder" block (LocalRunningCommands.tsx), which lists running commands rather than full history.
steps: Open a cloud session that has run a command (the Terminal section says "No commands have run in this session." when empty).
Open the "Changes" panel and go to "Terminal".
Turn on "Show exit codes" if you want exit status shown.
Compare the commands, their output and the exit status with Expected.
S66.17.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Terminal" section (list of commands) and the "Show exit codes" toggle

labels.text: The diff is too large to show in full.

S66.18.needs: a session where the agent changed files
S66.18.note: The diff body is rendered by DiffBody in CodeDiffFile (imported in LocalChangesPanel.tsx). Whether a click expands the diff in place was not confirmed from the code.
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files.
Open the "Changes" panel and click a file in the list.
Read the line-by-line diff shown for that file (added and removed lines).
Compare with Expected (a line-level diff of the agent's changes).
S66.18.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > click a changed file

S66.19.needs: a session where files were created, modified and deleted
S66.19.note: Labels come from CHANGE_STATE_LABELS in code-surface.ts; the file rows are rendered in LocalChangesPanel.tsx and CodeChangesPanel.tsx.
steps: Open a cloud session that has changed files.
Open the "Changes" panel.
Read the count line "N added, M removed" and the state word on each file row (Added, Modified, Deleted, Renamed, Untracked or Conflicted).
Compare which files are shown and their state with Expected (created, modified or deleted files).
S66.19.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel (heading "Changes", count "N added, M removed", then a row per file with its state)

S66.25.needs: none for reading the options; a running session is needed to see the effect
S66.25.note: There is no option called "edit mode" or "agent mode"; the closest control is this approval-policy menu plus the Plan option. Options and labels come from TOOL_APPROVAL_POLICY_OPTIONS.
steps: Open Code and look at the composer below the message box.
Click the approval/mode control (accessible name "Approval mode"; it shows "Plan" or the short label Ask, Auto or Skip).
Under the heading "Mode", read the options and their hints.
Pick one, then compare the choice and its hint with Expected (agent may act on its own, or asks first).
S66.25.where: Code > new session or open session > composer "Mode" control (the approval control, labelled "Approval mode") > choose one of "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking", "Skip approvals" or "Plan"

S66.26.needs: a running cloud or local session; a task that uses tools
S66.26.note: Enforcement of the chosen mode at runtime was not verified from the code, only the choice labels. Network labels come from the networkAccess list in code-surface.ts.
steps: Open the composer approval control and pick one option, for example "Ask before every action".
Start a task that needs a tool or a write, and see whether the agent waits for an approval card.
Change the option to "Skip approvals" and start another task.
Compare what the agent does with Expected (the chosen mode is honoured while the session runs).
S66.26.where: Code > composer "Approval mode" control > "Ask before every action" / "Run read-only actions without asking" / "Skip approvals"; network choice "Isolated", "Trusted hosts", "Full internet" in the environment settings

S66.27.needs: a session with some messages so a context figure exists
S66.27.note: The ring is UsageRing in CodeComposer.tsx (rendered near line 2162). Whether it shows before any message was not confirmed.
steps: Open a session in Code and type in the composer.
Look for the small ring icon near the composer (its accessible name is "Usage").
Click it and read the "Context window" value.
Compare the used amount with Expected (how much of the model context is used).
S66.27.where: Code > composer > the small usage ring (button named "Usage") > popover "Context window"

S66.28.needs: a signed-in account on a paid plan (the popover hides plan usage heading for free plans)
S66.28.note: Marked done in the audit. The popover is in CodeComposer.tsx (around lines 1562 and 1620), backed by useManagedUsageSummary.
steps: Open Code and find the "Usage" button in the composer.
Click it to open the popover.
Read "Plan usage limits" and the "Five hour limit" and "Weekly, all models" figures.
Click "See detailed breakdown" if you want more detail.
Compare the figures with Expected (plan usage or money spent is shown).
S66.28.where: Code > composer "Usage" button > popover "Plan usage limits" ("Five hour limit", "Weekly, all models", "Weekly, top model"); also the Usage settings page

S66.36.needs: a repository, a working branch and a GitHub connection; the feature is gated by the deployment (see the plan's switch-on note)
S66.36.note: On the desktop, the pull request form is in LocalPullRequest.tsx with "Push and open a pull request" and "Create branch and open pull request" (local-code.ts). The pull request number/link display was not fully traced.
steps: Open a session that has a repository and a working branch.
Open the "Changes" panel and click "Create pull request".
Wait for "Opening the pull request" to finish, then look for the pull request state (Merged, Closed without merging, Checks passing, Checks failing, Checks running).
Compare the number, link and state with Expected (session's pull request is shown).
S66.36.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Changes" panel > "Create pull request"; then the pull-request area shows status

S66.40.needs: a second account in the same workspace for Team, or any second signed-in account for Public
S66.40.note: The share dialog is CodeShareDialog.tsx and the shared view is SharedCodeSessionPage.tsx; the shared-page route is apps/web/app/code/shared/[token]/page.tsx. Shared viewers see a snapshot, as copy in code-surface.ts says.
steps: Open a cloud session.
Click the session actions button (accessible name "Session actions"), then click "Share".
In the "Share session" dialog, pick "Team" or "Public" under "Who can open this session".
Copy the link from the "Session link" field (copy button under the link).
Open the link in a private window signed in as another account and check that the session opens (the shared page is at /code/shared/[token]).
Compare with Expected (the other person can open it).
S66.40.where: Code > open a cloud session > "Session actions" icon menu > "Share" > dialog "Share session" > "Who can open this session" (Private, Team, Public) > "Done"
